limitations_and_boundaries: Theory assumes persistence time τ ≪ alpha-relaxation time τα; deviations appear when τ > τα.
Continuum elastic approximation valid only at low q.
Normal mode analysis restricted to thermal equilibrium in current experimental methods.
Model neglects cell–cell dissipation (wet vs. dry active materials) which could modify scalings.
Assumption of uncoordinated activity between cells; local alignment mechanisms not included.
Experimental correlation length sensitive to uncontrolled conditions; only qualitative features robust.
High-q peak disappearance in experiments not fully explained.
Simulations with division show additional tail in velocity distribution due to division algorithm.

experiments_or_tasks: Develop a linear response formalism for dense active matter by linearizing interaction forces around a mechanically stable configuration.
Project dynamics onto normal modes of the dynamical matrix to derive mode energy and velocity correlations.
Recast normal mode results into continuum elastic formulation to obtain Fourier-space velocity correlation function.

methods.name: Linear response theory
methods.protocol_description: Linearize interaction forces around a mechanically stable configuration (energy minimum) assuming persistence time τ ≪ alpha-relaxation time τα. Derive mode energy Eν = ζ v0^2 τ / [4 (1 + λν τ / ζ)] and Fourier velocity correlation 〈|v(q)|²〉 = Σν [v0² / (2(1 + λν τ / ζ))] |ξν(q)|².

methods.name: Continuum elastic formulation
methods.protocol_description: Map normal mode results to continuum elasticity with longitudinal and transverse correlation lengths ξL and ξT. Derive 〈|v(q)|²〉 = (N v0² / 2) [1/(1 + ξL² q²) + 1/(1 + ξT² q²)].

methods.name: Cell culture and imaging
methods.protocol_description: HCE-S cells plated in 12-well plate with DMEM/F12 Glutamax, 10% FBS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin. Incubated at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight to confluence. Before imaging, washed with PBS, medium replaced with HEPES-buffered medium. Imaged with phase-contrast Leica DM IRB at 37°C, 10× magnification, 10 min intervals, 1300×1000 pixels, ~48 h.

methods.name: Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV)
methods.protocol_description: Iterative PIV plugin for ImageJ, finest resolution level 3, 54×40 grid, 16 μm resolution. Extruded cells and nucleoli serve as tracer particles.

methods.name: Velocity correlation analysis
methods.protocol_description: Normalize velocity by instantaneous spatial mean-square average. Compute Fourier transform on PIV grid, then |ṽ(q)|². Fit to Eq. (16) with single parameter ξT, assuming (μ+B)/μ=4.3.

experiments_or_tasks: Compute velocity correlation functions, alpha-relaxation time, and compare with analytical predictions.
Simulate self-propelled Voronoi (SPV) model at dimensionless shape parameter p0=3.6 with open boundary conditions.
Simulate soft elastic particle model with overdamped active Brownian dynamics at packing fraction φ=1 and 30% polydispersity.

methods.name: Soft disk model simulation
methods.protocol_description: Overdamped active Brownian dynamics: ζ ṙ_i = v0 n̂_i - ∇_{r_i} V_i, with harmonic repulsion V_i = Σ_j (k/2) (σ_i + σ_j - |r_j - r_i|)² if within interaction range. Packing fraction φ=1, 30% polydispersity in radius. Time step δt=0.01, simulation length 5×10⁴ time units, first 1250 discarded.

methods.name: SPV model simulation
methods.protocol_description: Overdamped active Brownian dynamics with Voronoi-based cell shape energy V_i = (K/2)(A_i - A_0)² + (Γ/2)(P_i - P_0)². Dimensionless shape parameter p0=3.6, 30% variability in A_0. Open boundary conditions with boundary line tension λ=0.3. Time step δt=0.01, simulation length 5×10⁴ time units, first 1250 discarded.

methods.name: Velocity correlation computation
methods.protocol_description: Compute Fourier transform of particle velocities, then |v(q)|² = v(q)·v*(q), radial q average, and time average. For SPV, use cell center positions.

methods.name: Alpha-relaxation time computation
methods.protocol_description: Compute self-intermediate scattering function S(q,t) at q=2π/σ. τα is first time where S(q,t) < 0.5, bounded by simulation time.
